title: Props and Component Communication
subtitle: Pass information between React components using props.
description: Understand parent-child communication, reusable components, props, default values and how components share information.

blocks.text: PAGE 1 — Understand Props and Component Communication

Welcome to Lesson 3: Props and Component Communication. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “Props and Component Communication”. The goal is to pass information between React components using props.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.
Props are inputs passed from a parent component to a child. They let a component display different information without hard-coding every value inside the component.

blocks.question: A child component must display a different title for each course. What is the cleanest approach?
options: Hard-code a different child for every course.
Make every child read global state directly.
Pass the title as a prop from its parent.
Store the title in the CSS file.
blocks.explanation: Props make components reusable with different input data.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Props make components reusable with different input data.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Props make components reusable with different input data.

blocks.question: A child wants to tell its parent that a selection changed. What is a common React pattern?
options: Directly overwrite the parent component’s props.
Mutate the parent’s local variables from anywhere.
Duplicate the whole page.
Call a callback function the parent passed as a prop.
blocks.explanation: A callback lets the child request a parent-managed update without mutating props.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. A callback lets the child request a parent-managed update without mutating props.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. A callback lets the child request a parent-managed update without mutating props.

blocks.text: Treat props as read-only. When a child needs to request a change, it can call a callback provided by its parent rather than directly changing the parent’s data.

blocks.question: A component only needs the course title but receives a large unrelated object. What may improve clarity?
options: Pass only the relevant data or a clearly named prop.
Add more unrelated properties.
Rename the object to x.
Copy the object into every child.
blocks.explanation: Small, explicit interfaces make component dependencies easier to understand.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Small, explicit interfaces make component dependencies easier to understand.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Small, explicit interfaces make component dependencies easier to understand.

blocks.text: PAGE 3 — Apply it and check your reasoning
Use meaningful prop names and supply sensible defaults where appropriate. Avoid passing an entire large object if a component only needs one or two values.

blocks.question: A calculation is needed in three parts of the program. Which change reduces duplicated logic?
options: Copy the calculation to three new places.
Turn the result into a comment.
Create a focused function and call it with the required inputs.
Store the calculation in the page title.
blocks.explanation: A focused function centralizes the rule and lets the same behavior be tested once.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. A focused function centralizes the rule and lets the same behavior be tested once.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. A focused function centralizes the rule and lets the same behavior be tested once.

blocks.question: A function prints a total but another function needs to calculate with that total. What is usually required?
options: Return the total as a value.
Print the total in a larger font.
Rename the variable only.
Call the function repeatedly until the output is visible.
blocks.explanation: Printing is an output side effect; returning makes the value available to the caller.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Printing is an output side effect; returning makes the value available to the caller.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Printing is an output side effect; returning makes the value available to the caller.
